title: The Letter to the Philippians
lead: Paul's letter from prison to the church he founded in Philippi, a Roman colony in Macedonia. It is a letter of friendship and partnership, full of joy, and it holds the Christ hymn of 2:6-11, one of the earliest and most debated passages about who Jesus is.

sections.h: A letter from prison to partners
sections.b: Paul wrote to thank the Philippians for a gift brought by Epaphroditus, to report on his imprisonment, to send Timothy and Epaphroditus, to warn against opponents (most often read as teachers who demanded circumcision), and to urge unity, above all between two women co-workers, Euodia and Syntyche. Almost all scholars accept it as Paul's. Where he was held (Rome, Ephesus or Caesarea) and whether the letter joins two or three shorter letters are debated.

Philippians is the warmest of Paul's letters to churches. It shares themes with 2 Corinthians 8-9 (the generosity of the Macedonian churches), with Romans and Galatians (righteousness from God by faith, Philippians 3:9), and with 1 Corinthians 15 (the resurrection body, Philippians 3:21). Polycarp of Smyrna later wrote to the same church and recalled that Paul had written to them.
